verdict.rationale: Treasury's own docs say every movement of funds creates a Transaction object that serves as a ledger entry. They also document a `v2.money_management.transaction.created` event that fires when a flow creates a transaction, so there is a first-party event-driven ledger at its core. However, the evidence only covers transaction creation, not every state change, and says nothing about balance reads that reflect holds or pending activity. missing for 10: balance reads showing held/pending amounts, events for every transaction state transition (not just creation), explicit webhook endpoint registration/delivery docs for these events, independent or hands-on corroboration of real-time mirroring.

support.subject: As a developer, the ledger is real-time and event-driven — balance reads that reflect holds and pending activity, and webhooks for every transaction state change so my system mirrors the bank exactly

citations.quote: Every movement of funds into or out of a financial account creates a Transaction object. Transactions are the ledger entries for your financial accounts.
v2.money_management.transaction.created | A flow creates a transaction on a financial account.
Use transactions to build account activity feeds, reconcile against your internal systems, and track money movement through your platform.
